note: Curated demonstration incidents. Chosen for contrast (biome, spread regime, observation quality), not for good scores. Coordinates are a burning VIIRS cell on the init day; init = end of that UTC day. ML+physics replays need year >= 2024 (backend/ensemble.py refuses earlier years: no compatible blender fitted); earlier years are ML-only.

incidents.name: Flin Flon, Manitoba, Canada (boreal forest)
incidents.description: Late-May 2025 boreal wildfire complex on the Manitoba/Saskatchewan border that forced evacuations around Flin Flon. This is also the app's default demo event.
incidents.why_chosen: Boreal crown-fire regime with persistent smoke and variable cloud; the project's primary demo, so judges can compare the replay with the live forecast view.

availability.note: init day present, >= 3 following days with VIIRS cell-days in the window, observed new cells > 0

incidents.name: South Kalimantan, Indonesia (peatland, haze, ML-only)
incidents.description: October 2023 El Nino-driven peat and scrub fires in Kalimantan under thick haze.
incidents.why_chosen: Pre-2024, so no ML+physics blender exists: demonstrates the ML-only replay path. Also the most cloud-obscured case (proxy marks about 57-79% of the area as having no clear overpass on days 1-2), so false alarms on those days are largely unverifiable.

availability.note: init day present, >= 3 following days with VIIRS cell-days in the window, observed new cells > 0

incidents.name: Pantanal wetland-savanna, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil/Bolivia border
incidents.description: August 2024 dry-season fire activity in the Pantanal, part of the record 2024 South American fire season.
incidents.why_chosen: Savanna/grassland dry-season spread with a long-lived multi-day fire front, in a different hemisphere and fuel type from the Canadian cases.

availability.note: init day present, >= 3 following days with VIIRS cell-days in the window, observed new cells > 0

incidents.name: Punjab, India (agricultural stubble burning)
incidents.description: Post-harvest paddy-stubble burning season around the Punjab plains: hundreds of small, scattered, short-lived fires rather than one expanding front.
incidents.why_chosen: Mixed/agricultural case where 'spread' is mostly new independent ignitions, a stress test for a spread model; heavy smoke and haze season.

availability.note: init day present, >= 3 following days with VIIRS cell-days in the window, observed new cells > 0

incidents.name: Roraima, northern Brazil (savanna / forest edge, cloudy)
incidents.biome: savanna and forest edge, tropical cloud
incidents.description: March 2024 fire season in Roraima during the El Nino drought, when fires burned around Boa Vista and along the savanna/forest border.
incidents.why_chosen: Observation-limited case: the ERA5 cloud proxy marks a quarter to two-fifths of the area as having no clear overpass on days 1-2, so some 'false alarms' may simply be fire we could not see. The replay reports those separately as unverifiable.

availability.note: init day present, >= 3 following days with VIIRS cell-days in the window, observed new cells > 0

incidents.name: Smokehouse Creek area, Texas Panhandle, USA (prairie grass)
incidents.description: Wind-driven grass fires that started on 26 Feb 2024 and spread very fast the next day under dry, windy conditions.
incidents.why_chosen: Grass fire with an explosive second day: tests whether the system anticipates fast, wind-driven growth when the init-day footprint is small (19 burning cells at init).
